title: Iterative radix-2 divider + single shared 33x33 DSP multiplier (take DIV/REM off the EX critical path)
motivation:
Baseline Fmax is 5.44 MHz; the worst path (199.8 ns, 156 cells) is
clock -> u_fwd -> u_ex -> u_ex/u_alu -> u_ex, i.e. the forwarding mux feeding
the fully combinational 32-bit `/` and `%` array dividers (DIV, DIVU, REM,
REMU are four separate ~32-level subtract/compare arrays) and landing in the
EX/MEM register. CoreMark -O3 executes almost no divides inside the timed
region (list/matrix/state/crc kernels are add/shift/mul/branch), so a
multi-cycle divider costs essentially zero iterations/cycle while the Fmax
headroom is roughly an order of magnitude. The ALU also instantiates three
independent 64-bit multipliers (ss, uu, su) that burn DSP/LUT area and widen
the result mux.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
1. New rtl/divider.sv: sequential radix-2 restoring divider (one quotient bit
   per cycle, ~33-34 cycles incl. setup/fixup). On start it latches the
   post-forward rs1/rs2, the op (signed/unsigned, quotient/remainder), takes
   absolute values for signed ops, and iterates with a single 33-bit
   subtractor. Final cycle applies sign fixup (quotient negated iff
   a[31]^b[31] && b!=0 for signed; remainder takes sign of dividend) and
   registers the result. RV32M corner cases fall out naturally: x/0 gives
   quotient 0xFFFFFFFF and remainder = dividend; INT_MIN/-1 gives
   0x80000000 / 0. Under `RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` the same FSM/handshake is
   kept but with a short (1-2 cycle) latency returning the ALTOPS formula,
   so formal still exercises the stall path within the BMC depth.
2. rtl/alu.sv: drop the `/` and `%` operators entirely (DIV/REM ops no longer
   computed in the ALU). Replace mul_ss/mul_uu/mul_su with ONE 33x33 signed
   multiply: a_ext = {a[31] & a_signed, a}, b_ext = {b[31] & b_signed, b}
   (MUL/MULHU: both unsigned; MULH: both signed; MULHSU: a signed only),
   product[31:0] for MUL, product[63:32] for MULH/MULHU/MULHSU. This maps to
   a single Gowin DSP multiplier cascade instead of three.
3. rtl/ex_stage.sv: when ID/EX holds a valid DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU and the
   divider has not yet produced its result, assert a new `ex_busy` output:
   EX/MEM captures a bubble (valid=0, reg_write=0, mem_read/mem_write=0)
   while older instructions drain through MEM/WB normally. When the divider
   signals done, EX/MEM captures the divide result as alu_result (and all
   the usual RVFI fields: rs1_val/rs2_val are the latched post-forward
   operands), and the divider returns to idle. Start the divider only when
   not in a dmem stall so the forwarded operands are the final ones.
4. rtl/hazard_unit.sv / rtl/core.sv: add ex_busy as a stall source —
   stall_if and stall_id asserted (PC and ID/EX hold, NOT flushed), no
   redirect interaction needed because a divide never redirects and anything
   older than it is already past EX. dmem_stall keeps priority (EX/MEM holds).
5. test/test_alu.py: remove the combinational DIV/REM vectors from the
   `alu` toplevel (they move to the divider) and add test/test_divider.py
   with a clocked cocotb testbench (start/done handshake) covering all
   existing DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU vectors incl. /0, INT_MIN/-1, back-to-back
   divides, plus randomized vectors checked against Python semantics.
Measured evidence (proposer probe, `tools.eval.gowin` place_option 0 on a
scratch copy with DIV/REM simply removed from the ALU and the three
multipliers merged into one 33x33): Fmax 49.41 MHz (vs 5.44), logic 1971
LUT4 (vs 12312), 2 DSP. New worst paths (~25.5 ns) are regfile -> ID -> EX
branch compare -> IF redirect -> hazard -> ID/EX register, and regfile ->
EX ALU -> dmem; the multiplier is NOT on the critical path, so MUL stays
single-cycle. CoreMark objdump: the only div/rem instructions (5) are in
main(), outside the timed start/stop bracket, so the iterative divider costs
~0 iterations/cycle. The real implementation adds a small busy FSM to the
stall logic; keep ex_busy derived from registered divider state (not from
the forwarded operands) so it does not lengthen the redirect->hazard->ID
path. Expected fitness ~8x baseline (capped at +50 in the schema).

title: Split M-extension out of the 1-cycle EX ALU into a multi-cycle MUL/DIV unit that stalls the pipeline
motivation:
The baseline runs at only 5.44 MHz. The worst path (199.8 ns, 156 cells) is
clock -> u_fwd -> u_ex -> u_ex/u_alu -> u_ex. That is the forwarding mux
feeding the fully combinational 32-bit `/` and `%` operators in alu.sv.
They synthesize to a ~32-level ripple array of subtract/compare, and the
signed DIV/REM case adds pre- and post-negation around it. The same
combinational ALU also holds three separate 32x32->64 multipliers (mul_ss,
mul_uu, mul_su). Together these account for most of the 12.3k LUT4.
CoreMark at -O3 inside the timed window executes almost no DIV/REM and
only a few percent MUL (mostly core_matrix), so single-cycle M-ext costs
about 30x in Fmax to save a small number of cycles. No prior experiment
on this core (log.jsonl has only the baseline). The test_alu.py comment
mentions an earlier multi-cycle divider FSM (hyp-20260427-002) that was
reverted only by the v2 reset, not because it failed.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Take all eight M-extension ops out of the single-cycle ALU. Put them in a
new sequential unit `rtl/muldiv.sv` in the EX stage, with a start/busy/done
handshake that stalls the front of the pipeline while it works:

1. Divider: radix-2 restoring (or non-restoring) iteration on operand
   magnitudes, 1 quotient bit per cycle. About 32 iterations plus 1-2 setup
   and sign-fix cycles. Quotient and remainder are negated at the end.
   Special cases:
   - Divide by zero: force quotient = all ones and do NOT negate it. Set
     q_neg = (a_neg ^ b_neg) && (b != 0). The remainder then equals the
     dividend with no extra logic.
   - INT_MIN / -1: falls out of the magnitude algorithm
     (0x80000000 / 1 -> 0x80000000, remainder 0). Add a unit-test vector to
     prove it.
   Add a cheap early-out for b == 0 so those cases finish in 1 cycle.
2. Multiplier: replace the three 64-bit products with ONE 33x33 signed
   product. Sign-extend rs1 with (op is MULH/MULHSU) & a[31] and rs2 with
   (op is MULH) & b[31]. MUL takes [31:0]; MULH, MULHU and MULHSU take
   [63:32]. Operands are registered at start. The product goes into a
   result register one cycle later, so the Gowin DSP (MULT36X36 or
   composed 18x18) sits between flops and is never in series with the
   forwarding mux or the EX/MEM input. MUL* therefore costs 1-2 extra
   cycles.
3. Pipeline integration:
   - Add an `md_stall` input to hazard_unit, true while ID/EX holds a valid
     M-op and muldiv has not signalled done. During md_stall:
     - PC holds.
     - ID/EX holds (stall, no flush).
     - EX/MEM captures a BUBBLE (valid=0, reg_write=0, mem_read=0,
       mem_write=0) instead of the M-op. Add a small "bubble" path to the
       ex_stage register next to the existing hold path.
   - Older instructions in MEM and WB drain normally. Operands are latched
     from the post-forward rs1/rs2 on the first EX cycle, so draining
     those stages cannot corrupt them.
   - On done, EX/MEM captures the M-op with alu_result = md_result, and a
     `md_done` flag stops re-start until ID/EX advances.
   - When dmem_stall and md_stall are both active, dmem_stall wins (hold
     everything). The unit may keep iterating, but its result must be
     held until EX/MEM can accept it.
   - M-ops never redirect, so the redirect/flush paths are unchanged.
     Load-use detection still works: the M-op sits in ID/EX exactly like
     any other instruction.
4. alu.sv keeps only the RV32I ops (ADD/SUB/logic/SLT/shift/LUI). Its
   critical path becomes forward mux -> 32-bit add/shift -> EX/MEM. The
   next limiters should be that path and the branch-compare -> redirect ->
   PC/IF-flush path, which puts the core in the ~50-80 MHz range on GW2A.
5. Formal / ALTOPS:
   - Move the ALTOPS stand-in formulas into muldiv.sv under the same
     `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS`.
   - Keep the start/busy/done sequencing active under ALTOPS, but with a
     short fixed latency (for example 2-3 cycles instead of 32). The
     depth-20 insn/liveness/unique checks then still exercise the stall,
     bubble and hold logic.
   - The real (non-ALTOPS) build uses the full iterative divider.
   - rvfi_rs1/rs2_rdata must still report the latched post-forward operand
     values.

Expected result: Fmax goes from 5.44 MHz to at least ~40 MHz (7x or
more). CoreMark iter/cycle drops a few percent: about 1-2 stall cycles per
MUL and ~34 per DIV/REM, and the latter are nearly absent inside the timed
window. LUT4 should drop from 12.3k to roughly 4-5k because the array
divider and two of the three multipliers go away. Net fitness should rise
far more than the +50% cap on this field.

title: Fetch-stage branch prediction: bimodal BHT + predecoded B/J targets, zero-penalty JAL
motivation:
Fmax is pinned at ~5.4 MHz by the combinational divider path
(fwd_unit -> ex -> alu, 199.8 ns). Nothing in the front end comes close
to that, so on the current champion any IPC gained in fetch goes
straight into fitness at no Fmax cost. Today every taken branch and every
JAL/JALR resolves in EX. That kills the instruction in IF/ID and costs
one fetch slot (~0.78 cycles on average once the 22% imem stalls are
accounted for). CoreMark -O3 has about 18-20% conditional branches,
mostly taken loop back-edges plus data-dependent forward branches in
list/state/matrix code, and about 3-4% jumps. That puts roughly 0.12-0.15
taken control transfers on every retired instruction, or about 7-9% of
the ~1.6 CPI, lost to redirect bubbles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move the taken-path decision into the combined IF/ID cycle. The IF/ID
payload here is combinational (PC reg -> imem -> decode -> ID/EX), so a
prediction made while the instruction is in IF/ID steers the very next
fetch. A correctly predicted taken branch or JAL then costs 0 bubbles
instead of 1. Mispredictions still resolve in EX with the same 1-cycle
penalty as today.

Mechanism (all in the front end; the EX datapath is untouched except for the
redirect condition):
 1. Predecode io_imemData in if_stage: is_br = (opcode==1100011),
    is_jal = (opcode==1101111). Extract the B- and J-immediates and
    compute pred_target = pc + imm with a dedicated adder. The
    input comes from the imem-data flop and the output feeds the PC mux,
    so this path is far shorter than the divider.
 2. Direction: 256-entry bimodal table of 2-bit saturating counters
    indexed by pc[9:2]. Flops with synchronous reset to 2'b01 (weak
    not-taken) are preferred so Verilator/cosim are deterministic. Read
    combinationally from the PC register. (In ISS measurement 256 entries
    beat 128: 44k vs 54k mispredicts per 10 iterations.)
    pred_taken = imem_ready && !flush && !redirect &&
                 ((is_jal) || (is_br && bht[pc[9:2]][1]))
                 && (pred_target[1:0] == 2'b00)   // never predict a
                                                  // misaligned target;
                                                  // EX still traps it.
 3. PC update priority: reset > EX redirect > stall (hold) >
    pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4. Gating on !stall_if keeps load-use
    and dmem stalls correct: the same PC and instruction are refetched
    next cycle and predicted again.
 4. Carry pred_taken through if_id_t -> id_ex_t (flush clears it to 0).
 5. In ex_stage the redirect becomes a mispredict signal:
      br_mispred  = is_branch && (branch_taken != pred_taken)
      jal_mispred = is_jump && !is_jalr && !pred_taken
      jalr        = is_jalr                      (unchanged, always redirects)
      redirect    = (br_mispred || jal_mispred || jalr) && !misalign_fault
      redirect_target = is_jump ? jump_target
                      : branch_taken ? branch_target : pc + 4
    A branch predicted taken but actually not taken redirects to pc+4.
    pc_next, the RVFI fields and the trap logic are unchanged
    (architectural). The misaligned-target trap path stays correct:
    misaligned targets are never predicted, so pred_taken=0 there and EX
    behaves as today (trap, no redirect, pc_next = pc+4).
 6. BHT update in EX when in.valid && in.ctrl.is_branch && !stall_ex_mem
    (exactly once per branch, even under dmem-stall holds):
    saturating increment when taken, decrement when not, at in.pc[9:2].
    Pass the update port from ex_stage/core into if_stage.

Measured with the Python ISS (test/cosim/reference.py) over the timed
CoreMark region (10 iterations): 2,922,017 instructions, 529,588
conditional branches (294,425 taken), 49,367 JAL and 13,735 JALR.
Today's redirect bubbles total 357,527, or 0.122 per instruction.
With a 256-entry bimodal table plus fetch-time JAL (JALR still
resolved in EX), the bubbles fall to 58,001: 44,266 branch mispredicts
plus 13,735 JALR. That removes 299.5k bubbles, about 30k per
iteration. CoreMark takes about 449k cycles per iteration (12.12
iter/s at 5.442 MHz), and each removed bubble saves 0.78-1.0 cycles
(it overlaps with the 22% imem stalls). That is about 5.2-6.7% fewer
cycles.
Expected effect: JAL (about 1.7% of instructions, 100% predictable) and
loop back-edges become free. Bimodal gets roughly 85-90% direction
accuracy on CoreMark. The predictor only adds bubbles when it
predicts taken on a branch that is actually not taken, which costs the
same 1 cycle an unpredicted taken branch costs today. Net: remove
about 84% of the redirect bubbles, about 5-7% fewer cycles per
iteration, at unchanged Fmax (the critical path stays in the divider).
The cost is about 512 FF plus about 500-700 LUT4 for the table, adder
and muxes.

motivation:

gives one dominant loop (27.05 ns, all top-25 setup paths):
  regfile BSRAM CLKB->DO (2.26 ns tC2Q; Gowin mapped regs[] into block RAM,
  so ID/EX.rs*_val is the BSRAM output register)
  -> id_ex_w.rs2_val_*_s14 hold/bypass mux Gowin adds after the BSRAM
  -> 3 LUT levels of EX forward mux (rs2_*_s9/s8/s7, compares inline)
  -> 32-bit branch compare carry chain (u_ex/n330..n340)
  -> 1.7 ns net + 5 LUT levels in u_if (n330_s44..s0 = flush||redirect,
     fanout 102) = the NOP mux on out.instr
  -> rs1_addr_w (NOP-muxed rs1 field; feeds BSRAM read address AND hazard)
  -> u_hazard load-use compare -> stall_id/flush_id (4 LUTs, fanout 33)
  -> ID/EX rs*_val D/RESET and PC CE.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Four timing-only changes with cycle-identical behaviour (the cosim cycle count
must stay 4,491,817):
1. Raw fetch word into ID. if_stage drives out.instr = imem_data unmuxed and
   keeps out.valid = !(imem_stall || redirect). Regfile read addresses,
   decoder, imm_gen and hazard_unit's load-use compare all use the raw word.

   only needs imem_ready, because a capture with redirect=1 never happens:
   flush_id=1, or else dmem_stall makes stall_id=1. So redirect feeds only
   the PC mux and flush_id. Equivalence: with redirect=1, load_use is a
   don't-care (see above). With imem_stall=1 and a spurious load_use,
   "capture an invalid NOP" becomes "flush to bubble", which is the same
   bubble with the same PC hold. load_use can never coincide with ex_busy
   (LOAD vs DIV in ID/EX), so a DIV is never flushed.

   "distributed_ram" *) and drop the reset-clears-all loop, because LUT-RAM
   cannot be reset and a reset loop blocks RAM inference. RISC-V leaves GPRs

The champion (hyp-20260928-001-r1s0, 45.3 MHz, 100.91 iter/s) is now limited by
one control chain that covers two pipeline stages in a single cycle
(critical path 27.0 ns, 28 cells: u_id -> u_ex -> u_if -> u_hazard -> u_id,
ending at id_ex.rs1_val):
  ID/EX reg -> forward_unit 5-bit rd==rs compares -> 3:1 forward mux ->
  32-bit branch compare -> redirect -> if_stage `out.instr = redirect ? NOP
  : imem_data` -> rs1/rs2 field -> regfile async read + write-first bypass
  AND hazard_unit load-use compare -> stall_id/flush_id -> ID/EX
  enable / sync-reset on ~230 flops.
So the EX-stage branch decision gates the instruction word that feeds
decode, the register-file read, and the load-use detector in the same
cycle. In a 5-stage in-order pipeline these should be independent
paths. The IPC is already good (~2.23 CoreMark/MHz); the lever now is
Fmax, and this chain sets it.

make squashing a valid-bit kill, so no EX-stage result feeds the ID

   regfile read addresses and the load-use comparator all use raw
   io_imemData. if_id.valid = imem_ready (a flop in the bench) and carries
   the squash information. Redirect cycles do not need the NOP: the redirect
   already has priority on the PC and kills ID/EX (see 2). A spurious load-use
   match on a wrong-path or not-ready word only turns into a bubble in a slot
   that is already a bubble. Gate load_use with imem_ready so an
   imem-stall word cannot hold a live ID/EX.

2. Valid-bit squash instead of whole-register sync reset (id_stage).
   ID/EX datapath fields (pc, rs*_val, imm, rd, rs*_addr, instr, alu_op,
   ...) get only a clock enable = !(dmem_stall || load_use || ex_busy).
   Every term comes from registered state or the raw fetch word.
   Redirect / load-use / not-ready only clear the small set of
   side-effect bits {valid, reg_write, mem_read, mem_write, is_branch,
   is_jump, is_illegal}. So the path branch-compare -> redirect ends at
   about 7 flop D-inputs through one AND level, not at 230 flop SR/CE pins.
   Keep the synchronous `reset` on every ID/EX field. Reset comes from a
   port, not from logic, so it adds no depth. A killed slot keeps its stale
   rd/data, but reg_write=0 and valid=0, so it never forwards, writes, or
   retires. The EX-side divider `is_div` must stay qualified by in.valid.

3. Registered forwarding selects computed in ID (id_stage + forward_unit).
   While an instruction is in ID, compare its rs1/rs2 with (a) the rd of
   the instruction currently in ID/EX, which will be in EX/MEM when this one
   executes -> sel EX_MEM, and (b) the rd of the instruction currently in
   EX/MEM, which will be in MEM/WB -> sel MEM_WB. Qualify each with that
   stage's reg_write && valid && rd!=0. Register the result into ID/EX as
   one-hot selects. The ID-time regfile read, whose write-first bypass
   covers the MEM/WB->regfile case, gives the default. In EX the forward
   mux select is a flop output, so the 5-bit comparators leave the EX path.
   Stall cases stay correct:

       data (hold_wb), so the relative distances do not change;
     - a load-use bubble re-evaluates the consumer in ID next cycle;
     - ex_busy: the divider latches operands on its first cycle,
       when the selects are still exact, as today.

title: Port the bimodal BHT + fetch-time B/JAL predictor onto the divider champion, keeping the mispredict redirect off the load-use/ID-stall path
motivation:
hyp-003-r1s2 measured a 6.65% cycle reduction (4,491,817 -> 4,193,175
cycles for 10 timed CoreMark iterations, i.e. +7.1% iter/cycle) from a
256-entry bimodal BHT with predecoded B/J targets and zero-bubble JAL.
It was built on the divider-bound 5.4 MHz baseline, so it lost to 001.
The gain is orthogonal to 001 and has not yet been ported onto it
(LESSONS.md). The ISS breakdown shows 357.5k redirect bubbles in the timed
region. Bimodal+JAL removes 299.5k of them. The remaining 44k branch
mispredicts + 13.7k JALR are <1% of cycles, so a fancier direction
predictor (gshare, RAS) is not worth its timing risk. What matters is
landing the known +7.1% IPC without losing more than ~2.3% Fmax (the
acceptance bar is +4.6%).
On 001 (45.3 MHz) the critical path is 27.0 ns / 20 levels:
ID/EX -> forward mux -> branch compare -> redirect -> IF NOP-mux of the
fetched instr -> hazard load-use rs1/rs2 compare -> stall_id/flush_id ->
ID/EX register enable (u_id > u_ex > u_if > u_hazard > u_id). A naive
port puts XOR-with-prediction and a 3-way target mux on exactly that
path. In core_bench_si.sv, io_imemData comes straight from an LFSR flop,
so the new predecode -> pc+imm adder -> PC path starts at a register and
is much shorter than the redirect path.

motivation:

place_option 0) shows that ALL top-25 setup paths belong to one family
(21.3-22.0 ns arrival):

  -> EX one-hot forward AND-OR (rs1_31_s0) -> alu_a/alu_b mux
  -> u_alu mul_a sign-ext -> 33x33 DSP product mul_p (3.76 ns)

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Three cycle-neutral timing cuts. The cosim cycle count must stay at
4,491,817. All of them were prototyped and timed by the proposer:
1. AGU. Add EX/MEM field `mem_addr`, captured from `jalr_sum` (rs1 + imm,
   where rs1 is the one-hot forward mux output; it does not go through
   alu_a/alu_b or the ALU case). mem_stage uses in.mem_addr for
   io_dmemAddr, byte_mask, mem_misalign, the load shift amount and RVFI
   aligned_addr. EX/MEM.alu_result keeps the full result and is used only
   for forwarding and WB. Loads and stores already compute ALU_ADD rs1+imm,
   so the RVFI and cosim values are identical.
2. Pre-muxed WB data. mem_stage computes wb_data = ctrl.mem_to_reg ?
   load_data : in.alu_result and registers it into MEM/WB (held under
   hold_wb like the other data fields). wb_stage drives w_data = in.wb_data.
   This removes the u_wb LUT that heads every MEM/WB->EX forward path and the
   regfile write-first bypass. The extra mux sits on the short
   BSRAM-DO -> load-extract -> MEM/WB path.
3. MUL merged at the last EX result-mux level. Compute the 33x33 signed
   product in ex_stage (or as a separate alu output) from the *forwarded*
   rs1/rs2 directly, bypassing the alu_a/alu_b immediate/AUIPC muxes. Take
   the MUL arms out of the ALU op case. The EX/MEM alu_result D input
   becomes the one-hot AND-OR
     ({32{sel_lo}} & mul_p[31:0]) | ({32{sel_hi}} & mul_p[63:32])
     | ({32{!(sel_lo|sel_hi)}} & (is_jump ? pc+4 : is_div ? div_result : alu_out))
   with sel_lo = (alu_op==MUL) and sel_hi = (alu_op in MULH/MULHU/MULHSU),
   both decoded from ID/EX flops, off the critical path. This leaves the
   DSP output 2 LUT levels from the flop instead of 7.
   Under `RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS`, sel_lo and sel_hi are tied to 0 and the
   ALTOPS MUL formulas stay in the ALU case, so formal behaviour is unchanged.

In the prototype, one path family still reached the dmem BSRAM through
an ex_result -> `dmem_addr_c_*` cell. Make sure the mem_addr register D is
really jalr_sum: use a separate always_ff, and if needed a
`/* synthesis syn_keep=1 */` on the jalr_sum net or mem_addr register so
Gowin cannot share it with the ALU adder. The residual paths are ~13.6-13.8 ns

title: Restructure the EX datapath: ID-stage distance-2 bypass (no WB->EX forward), dedicated AGU for dmem address, one-hot parallel result select
motivation:
The champion (001-r2s0, 59.08 MHz, 4.49M cycles) has a 22.0 ns, 12-cell critical path:
MEM/WB.ctrl.mem_to_reg flop -> WB mux (mem_to_reg ? read_data : alu_result)
-> 3-source EX forward AND-OR -> alu_b mux -> ALU adder -> 19-arm case(op)
output mux -> EX/MEM result mux (is_jump ? pc+4 : is_div ? div : alu)
-> dmem BSRAM input (dmem_1_dmem_1_0_0_s). In fpga/core_bench_si.sv the dmem
is an async-read 2048x32 array that Gowin maps to BSRAM by absorbing the
EX/MEM.alu_result flop as the BSRAM address register, so the load/store
address is computed through the whole ALU result tree and then has to meet
BSRAM address setup. Roughly half of those 12 levels are there only because of
how the datapath is arranged: a WB-stage mux sits in front of forwarding,
the forward mux has three sources, and the memory address goes through the
general ALU output mux and the jump/div result mux even though it is
always rs1+imm. Every other EX path (branch compare -> redirect -> PC,
shifter/MUL -> EX/MEM) starts with the same WB-mux + 3-way forward prefix.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Rebuild the EX datapath in three coordinated, cycle-neutral parts. CoreMark
cycle count stays at 4,491,817. All the gain comes from Fmax.

(1) Drop the WB->EX forwarding source. The distance-2 bypass moves into ID.
When an instruction is captured into ID/EX, if its rs matches the
producer now in EX/MEM (MEM stage, rd!=0, wb_reg_write after the misalign
trap), rs?_val captures that producer's MEM-stage result
mem_res = mem_to_reg ? load_data : alu_result (this is today's WB mux, one
stage earlier). Otherwise it captures the regfile read, which keeps the
write-first bypass that covers distance 3. MEM/WB registers that
single value as wb_data, so the regfile write data and write-first bypass
start at a flop. The EX operand mux becomes a 2:1 select, a single LUT3:
fwd_sel ? EX/MEM.alu_result : ID/EX.rs?_val. It is registered one-hot in ID
as today (distance-1 match on ID/EX.rd with reg_write && !is_jump).
This is safe under every stall: ID/EX only captures when stall_id=0. For a
LOAD in MEM that means dmem_ready=1, so load_data is valid, which is the same
condition under which MEM/WB captures it today. Load-use still costs exactly
one bubble, because the consumer is captured from the LOAD's MEM-stage data
in the next cycle. The only case where ID/EX holds while EX/MEM advances is
ex_busy, and the divider has already latched its operands then. The
hold_mem_wb data-retention hack is no longer needed for correctness. Keep
clearing valid on hold.

(2) Add a dedicated AGU in EX: agu = rs1_fwd + imm, with its own adder and no
alu_src, alu_op or result muxes. It is registered into a new EX/MEM.mem_addr
field that drives io_dmemAddr, the byte mask, the misalign check, the load
shift and the RVFI mem_addr. The BSRAM-absorbed address register is then fed
by: flop -> LUT3 forward -> carry chain (only bits [12:2] reach the BSRAM).
EX/MEM.alu_result keeps the full result for forwarding and write-back, and it
now ends at an ordinary flop instead of BSRAM setup.

(3) Replace case(op) plus the separate is_jump/is_div result mux with
parallel functional units and a one-hot result select. ID decodes and
registers the selects in ID/EX:
res_sel = {ADD (add/sub/lui/auipc share one adder, with registered sub and
a_is_pc/a_is_zero bits), LOGIC (and/or/xor with a registered 2-bit sub-select),
SLT/SLTU, SHIFT, MUL_LO, MUL_HI, PC4 (jal/jalr), DIV}.
Also register the MUL sign-extend bits (a_signed, b_signed) and the shift
direction/arith bits so that no EX logic decodes the 5-bit alu_op.
EX then computes result = OR over k of ({32{res_sel[k]}} & unit_k): two LUT4
levels, where today the 19-arm case mux plus result mux takes 3 to 5.
The ALTOPS substitutions for MUL* are kept on the MUL_LO/MUL_HI units under
the same `ifdef`. ALTOPS for DIV/REM stays in divider.sv.

Expected effect: removing the WB mux and one forward level from all EX paths
(~2 cells), and the ALU case/result mux from the dmem-address path (~3-4
cells), should cut the 12-cell BSRAM path to about 5-6 cells. The next
limiters would be the shifter/MUL -> one-hot OR -> EX/MEM.alu_result path and
branch compare -> redirect -> PC/flush_id, and both of these also lose the
2-cell forwarding prefix. At the champion's ~1.8 ns/cell a ~17-18 ns worst
path would give ~56 -> ~65-70 MHz, i.e. +10-18% at unchanged cycles. The new
MEM-side path is BSRAM tCO (~2.3 ns) -> load shift/sext -> mem_res mux ->
ID capture mux -> ID/EX.rs_val, about 5 cells. That stays well under the target.

lesson: - 2026-09-28 hyp-20260928-002-r3s1 (improvement, +48.66%): Moving the distance-2 bypass into the ID/EX capture is cycle-neutral and safe. ID/EX captures mem_res = mem_to_reg ? load_data : alu_result only when stall_id=0, so a MEM-stage load has dmem_ready. The only case where ID/EX holds while EX/MEM advances is ex_busy, and the divider has already latched its operands then. This leaves a 2:1 LUT3 as the EX forward, and together with the rs1+imm AGU and the registered one-hot result select it reached 87.4 MHz, against 65-70 MHz predicted. The forecast was low because Gowin path "ns" is arrival time that includes a fixed ~5.1 ns clock-insertion offset (27.05 ns = 45.3 MHz, 22.0 ns = 59.1 MHz, 16.74 ns = 87.4 MHz), so Fmax ≈ 1000/(arrival - 5.1). Cutting arrival by 24% therefore raised Fmax by 48%; always subtract the offset before scaling. The next limiters are balanced at ~16.7 ns: EX/MEM.alu_result -> 2:1 fwd -> ALU -> one-hot OR -> alu_result (7 cells), and fwd -> branch-compare carry chain -> redirect -> PC (29 cells), so the next cut has to shorten both.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion is hyp-001-r2s0: 59.08 MHz and 4,491,817 timed cycles. Every
taken branch and every JAL still resolves in EX and kills the fetch slot
in IF/ID. The r1s2 cosim measured 357.5k redirect bubbles in the timed
region. A 256-entry bimodal BHT plus predecoded B/J targets and zero-bubble
JAL removed 299.5k of them, giving 4,193,175 cycles (-6.65% cycles,
+7.1% iter/cycle). r2s2 then ported this onto the older 45 MHz core
(001-r1s0) and saw no visible Fmax cost (48.4 MHz, the same as the
hazard-only cut). It lost only because 001-r2s0's fuller loop cut reached
59 MHz in the same round. LESSONS.md says the next step is to port the
predictor onto 001-r2s0 and re-time it, because at 59 MHz the redirect
path and the fetch predecode->adder->PC path have less slack.
The champion's worst path is MEM/WB -> WB mux -> EX forward mux -> ALU ->
dmem BSRAM address (the absorbed EX/MEM alu_result register), 12 cells.
The branch compare -> redirect -> PC/flush path runs next to it with about
the same depth. So the port must add no logic level to
compare -> redirect. The r2s2 design put an XOR with pred_taken on that
path, which is the risk here. This hypothesis removes that XOR entirely.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Port the r1s2/r2s2 predictor, which has a known +7.1% iter/cycle, onto
the r2s0 champion. Restructure it so that every prediction-dependent term
is either a registered bit in ID/EX or lies on a path that starts at a
flop (PC reg, imem-data flop) and ends at the PC reg, well below the
ALU->dmem path.

A. Fetch-side prediction (if_stage.sv). The IF/ID bundle is
   combinational, so a prediction here steers the very next fetch.
   - Predecode raw imem_data: is_br = opcode==1100011,
     is_jal = opcode==1101111. Select the B- or J-immediate by one opcode
     bit, and compute pred_target = pc + imm_bj with a dedicated adder.
     Keep the pc+4 incrementer separate; do NOT share one adder with a
     muxed operand, because that would put the BHT read in front of the
     carry chain.
   - Bimodal BHT: 256 x 2-bit saturating counters indexed by pc[9:2],
     read combinationally from the PC register. Prefer
     (* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *) LUT-RAM (async read, 1 sync
     write port, no reset). A misprediction only costs performance and
     Verilator zero-initialises, so cosim stays deterministic. If Gowin
     will not infer LUT-RAM for it, use plain flops with no reset
     (or reset to 2'b01 if a formal/cosim check needs it).
   - pred_taken = (is_jal || (is_br && bht_rd[1])) && !imm_bj[1].
     The PC is always 4-aligned, so imm_bj[1] is exactly the
     misaligned-target test, and EX still traps misaligned targets.
     Do NOT gate pred_taken with redirect, imem_ready or flush. On a
     redirect the PC mux takes redirect_target and ID/EX is flushed. On
     an imem stall stall_if holds the PC and ID/EX captures ctrl=0.
     In both cases the predicted value is a don't-care. This follows the
     r2s0 lesson: keep redundant control signals off the datapath.
   - PC mux priority: reset > redirect > stall_if (hold) >
     pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4. Redirect stays the last mux
     level. A held instruction is simply refetched and predicted again,
     so load-use, dmem stalls and the divider need no special handling.
   - Export pred_taken and alt_target = pred_taken ? pc+4 : pred_target
     in if_id_t. alt_target is where a mispredicted B-type goes.
B. ID (id_stage.sv, core_pkg.sv). Register the following into ID/EX with
   the existing stall/flush discipline. flush clears only the control
   bits, as in r2s0.
   - pred_taken.
   - alt_target (32 flops). This is the full mispredict target of a
     conditional branch, so EX no longer needs pc+imm or a
     pred-dependent mux on the redirect path.
   - Branch sense folded with the prediction:
     ctrl.branch_op <= funct3 ^ {2'b00, pred_taken}.
     BEQ/BNE, BLT/BGE and BLTU/BGEU are complement pairs that differ only
     in funct3[0]. So cond(branch_op_eff) == (actual_taken != pred_taken)
     is exactly the mispredict condition, computed by the same comparator
     and case-mux as today.
   - br_redir_ok = is_branch && !imm[1]. A branch with a misaligned target
     is never predicted taken, and if it is taken it traps without
     redirecting.
   - jal_unpred = is_jal && !pred_taken && !imm[1]. This should never be
     1, but keep it as a registered safety term so the redirect is
     correct under any symbolic stream.
   - pred_taken, br_redir_ok and jal_unpred are control bits. Like
     ctrl_q, they are zeroed on flush and on an invalid (imem-stalled)
     capture, because an invalid capture holds a garbage fetch word
     that may decode as a branch. They must never assert redirect for a
     bubble.
C. EX (ex_stage.sv):
   - mispred_cond = the existing branch case-mux on in.ctrl.branch_op
     (now the folded sense). The logic is unchanged.
   - redirect = (in.br_redir_ok && mispred_cond)
                || (in.ctrl.is_jalr && !misalign_jalr)
                || in.jal_unpred.
     JAL never redirects from EX, and misalign_jalr depends only on
     jalr_sum[1] (rs1[1:0]+imm[1:0]). The compare -> redirect depth stays
     the same as today's branch_taken -> redirect.
   - redirect_target = in.ctrl.is_jalr ? {jalr_sum[31:1],1'b0}
                                       : in.alt_target.
     Neither input depends on the compare.
   - Architectural fields stay exact and off the timed path:
     branch_taken = in.ctrl.is_branch && (mispred_cond ^ in.pred_taken).
     pc_next, misalign traps, ctrl_with_trap and JAL/JALR rd = pc+4 are
     all unchanged (pc_next and branch_target are RVFI-only and get pruned).
     The misalign_branch trap uses branch_taken && in.imm[1].
D. BHT update from the EX/MEM register, not from EX. The update has
   en = ex_mem.valid && ex_mem.ctrl.is_branch, idx = ex_mem.pc[9:2] and
   taken = ex_mem.branch_taken. A branch sits in EX/MEM for exactly one
   cycle (EX/MEM holds only on a dmem stall, which needs a mem op in
   EX/MEM), so each branch updates exactly once. This takes the comparator
   -> counter -> 256-way write path out of EX. The one-cycle-later update
   costs a negligible number of mispredicts in tight loops.
E. core.sv: wire the EX/MEM update port to u_if and pass the new fields.
   Hazard/forward units are unchanged (they already read the raw fetch word).

Expected result: the timed cycle count falls from 4,491,817 to about
4.19-4.21M (r1s2 measured 4,193,175 with EX-time update), which is
+6.7-7.1% iter/cycle. The new logic lies on flop->PC paths
(lfsr/imem -> predecode -> adder -> PC, and PC -> BHT read -> PC-mux select),
each about 8-11 ns against the 16.9 ns period. The compare->redirect path
keeps its current depth. Fmax should therefore stay about 57-60 MHz and
fitness should land around 139-141 (+6-7%).
Implementer checks:
(1) The cosim cycle count must drop to about 4.2M. If it does not,
    prediction is not taking effect.
(2) `make timing TARGET=bench` should show the worst path is still
    ALU->dmem. If PC -> BHT read shows up, shrink the BHT to 128 entries
    (about 0.2% extra cycles) or put it in LUT-RAM.
(3) Run formal: pc_fwd/pc_bwd/liveness/unique must pass. pc_wdata is
    still the architectural next PC.

changes.description: Add pred_taken and alt_target[31:0] to if_id_t. Add pred_taken, alt_target, br_redir_ok and jal_unpred to id_ex_t. Add a comment explaining that id_ex.ctrl.branch_op carries funct3 ^ {2'b00,pred_taken}, the mispredict sense.

Predecode B/JAL on raw imem_data. Add a dedicated pc+imm_bj adder (separate from pc+4). Add a 256x2 bimodal BHT (LUT-RAM preferred, else flops), read at pc[9:2], with a write port driven from EX/MEM (en/idx/taken, saturating +/-1). pred_taken = (is_jal || is_br && ctr[1]) && !imm_bj[1], with no redirect/imem_ready gating. PC priority: reset > redirect > stall > (pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4). Export pred_taken and alt_target = pred_taken ? pc+4 : pred_target.

Register pred_taken, alt_target, br_redir_ok = is_branch && !imm[1] and jal_unpred = is_jal && !pred_taken && !imm[1] into ID/EX. Control bits are cleared on flush and alt_target is a data flop. Register ctrl.branch_op = funct3 ^ {2'b00, pred_taken}, so EX's comparator directly computes 'mispredicted'.

redirect = (br_redir_ok && cond(branch_op_eff)) || (is_jalr && !jalr_sum[1]) || jal_unpred. redirect_target = is_jalr ? jalr_target : alt_target. Neither depends on the compare beyond the existing single-level redirect OR. Architectural branch_taken = is_branch && (cond ^ pred_taken) feeds pc_next, the misalign trap (branch_taken && imm[1]) and ex_mem.branch_taken for the BHT update. Keep RVFI pc_next/rd_wdata/trap semantics exactly as before.
Wire the BHT update port (ex_mem_w.valid && ex_mem_w.ctrl.is_branch, ex_mem_w.pc[9:2], ex_mem_w.branch_taken) into u_if. Top-level IO and RVFI are unchanged; hazard/forward wiring is unchanged.

cocotb pipeline tests. A warm backward BNE loop retires with continuous pc_rdata/pc_wdata and no redirect bubbles after warm-up. JAL retires with no bubble. A branch predicted taken but actually not taken falls through to pc+4 (tests the folded branch sense for all 6 funct3). A predicted-not-taken branch that is taken goes to its target. Misaligned-target JAL/branch still traps with pc_wdata=pc+4. Load-use, imem-stall and dmem-stall on a predicted branch keep rvfi_order/PC continuity. A DIV behind a predicted branch completes.
